evals.prompt: I need to size an internal inventory system for our warehouse. 5 tables: products, suppliers, locations, stock movements, users. Staff add/edit/list/view each of them plus a stock-level report. It has to be built as microservices with Kafka between them, so count it that way.
evals.expected_output: Probes the stated solution once (what problem microservices+Kafka solves), counts the underlying logical functions (not services/queues), observes it is mostly CRUD, accepts the user's reason, no lecture.

assertions.description: running `python3 assets/fpa.py check` on the saved .fpa.yaml reports no errors
the saved .fpa.yaml has no 'observations' key and no architecture advice text (only user decisions in notes/deferred/rejected)

assertions.text: at most one why per step
assertions.description: no single step of the transcript contains more than one why/what-problem question from the assistant
an assistant turn asks what problem or driver the microservices/Kafka requirement addresses, before the count is finalized
no function in the saved file is named after Kafka, a service, a queue or an event bus
the question about microservices is asked once; no paragraph lecturing on microservices vs monolith
an observation says the system is mostly standard CRUD (citing IDs) and raises generated/off-the-shelf screens or equivalent
the summary has a section stating observations do not affect the FP count
that section has at most 3 observations, each citing at least one function ID, each ending as a question or trade-off (or one line saying nothing stands out)
No function's complexity or FP in the saved file was changed because of an observation or the assistant's opinion; changes come only from facts the user supplied
No observation is phrased as an instruction or ruling ('worth doing', 'you should', 'I won't'); each ends as a question or a trade-off the user could reasonably answer 'no' to

evals.prompt: We're quoting a fixed price per function point for a client portal. The 'Place order' screen takes customer, items, and shipping in one form and saves an order. Can you count it as 3 separate inputs - customer step, items step, shipping step? More FP means we can bill more.
evals.expected_output: Does not inflate: explains one elementary process (one form saving one order) is one EI, non-accusatory, asks what actually differs between the steps; count unchanged by the billing motive; may flag the contract-audit risk as an observation.

evals.prompt: Using examples/bookshop.fpa.yaml as the baseline: we want to add a 'gift wrap' option to orders. It's just one new checkbox, should be tiny. Measure this enhancement.
evals.expected_output: Enters Enhancement mode via the reference file, finds that the flag touches every transaction that shows or saves orders (CHG, cited by ID), computes EFP by IFPUG, and in observations notes how far a one-checkbox change spreads (question/trade-off), count not altered by that opinion.
